abstract_sentences.text: Causal discovery with latent variables is a fundamental task.
Yet most existing methods rely on strong structural assumptions, such as enforcing specific indicator patterns for latents or restricting how they can interact with others.

We argue that a core obstacle to a general, structural-assumption-free approach is the lack of an equivalence characterization: without knowing what can be identified, one generally cannot design methods for how to identify it.
In this work, we aim to close this gap for linear non-Gaussian models.

evidence.anchor: close this gap for linear non-Gaussian models

abstract_sentences.text: We establish the graphical criterion for when two graphs with arbitrary latent structure and cycles are distributionally equivalent, that is, they induce the same observed distribution set.

evidence.anchor: graphical criterion ... same observed distribution set

abstract_sentences.text: Key to our approach is a new tool, edge rank constraints, which fills a missing piece in the toolbox for latent-variable causal discovery in even broader settings.
We further provide a procedure to traverse the whole equivalence class and develop an algorithm to recover models from data up to such equivalence.

To our knowledge, this is the first equivalence characterization with latent variables in any parametric setting without structural assumptions, and hence the first structural-assumption-free discovery method.

evidence.anchor: first equivalence characterization ... without structural assumptions

abstract_sentences.text: Code and an interactive demo are available at https://equiv.cc.

method_analysis.formal_objects: Digraph G with observed X and latent L; B weighted adjacency, A=(I−B)^{-1}, observed mixing A_X,:, support Q(G), path rank ρ_G, edge rank r_G, matching rank mrank, children bases, and matroid solution sets colaug.
method_analysis.input_output: Given observed distribution p(X), glvLiNG estimates A via OICA; input rank queries yield a support matrix/digraph G̃; output is the full irreducible equivalence class and its optional CP(G) presentation.
method_analysis.complexity_statement: The paper provides empirical runtime and says Phase 2 decomposes into independent singleton columns; it does not give a single asymptotic complexity theorem for full glvLiNG in the main text.
method_analysis.algorithm_count: No captioned Algorithm object appears; the pipeline and two phases are prose/boxed problem descriptions.

evidence.anchor: Procedure of reduction to the irreducible form

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Remove non-ancestors and merge maximal redundant latent sets while adding induced parent-to-child edges.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any latent-variable digraph.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 1
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Distributional equivalence iff observed mixing sets agree up to column scaling and permutation.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two irreducible models with shared observed variables.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 2

evidence.anchor: Path rank constraints in mixing matrices

equation_theory_inventory.summary: For generic A, each observed-row mixing submatrix rank equals the corresponding path rank.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Generic graph-compatible invertible mixing matrix.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Omitted; attributed to prior work and Appendix B.5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 3
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Equivalence iff a vertex permutation preserves all path ranks from arbitrary source sets to observed target sets.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two irreducible models.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 4

evidence.anchor: Edge rank constraints in support matrices

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Matching rank of every support submatrix equals the corresponding edge rank.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any digraph and vertex subsets.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Omitted; immediate from Definition 6 and Appendix B.5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 1

evidence.anchor: Duality between path ranks and edge ranks

equation_theory_inventory.summary: A complement identity equates path-rank deficiency with dual edge-rank deficiency.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any digraph; overlapping Z,Y allowed.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Omitted; existing matroid result, Appendix B.5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 5
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Equivalence iff a vertex permutation preserves all edge ranks for source sets containing L.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two irreducible models.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Omitted; direct re-expression and Appendix B.5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 2
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Equivalence is characterized by equality of children-bases for L and for every singleton latent-plus-observed source set, up to permutation.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two irreducible models; bases as in Eq.18.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: glvLiNG rank realization uses the same singleton decomposition; p.10 and Appendix A.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 6
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Reversing any collection of vertex-disjoint simple cycles with the induced incident-edge rewiring preserves equivalence.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any digraph; cycles vertex-disjoint.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Omitted; prior result and Appendix B.5.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 7
equation_theory_inventory.summary: An absent edge is admissibly added exactly when its target is a coloop in the relevant latent-source matching matroid; deletion is reversible.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Irreducible model; edge absent before addition.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: Equivalence traversal step in glvLiNG; p.9–10.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 3

evidence.anchor: Transformational characterization of the equivalence class

equation_theory_inventory.summary: All equivalent irreducible digraphs are connected by admissible edge additions/deletions and at most one cycle reversal, up to latent relabeling.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two irreducible equivalent models.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: BFS/DFS traversal of recovered class; p.9 and Appendix A.4.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 4
equation_theory_inventory.summary: CP(G) contains solid and dashed edges, is maximal within the edge-operation component, and captures its intersection of must-appear edges.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Irreducible model; one cycle-reversal configuration.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Statement and properties in Appendix C.3; no separate proof block.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 8

evidence.anchor: How the transversal matroid changes when augmenting more sources

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Independent sets of a horizontal matrix concatenation are unions of independent sets from the two blocks.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Two binary matrices with disjoint source columns.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 9

evidence.anchor: Reducing all union equivalence checks to singleton checks

equation_theory_inventory.summary: All matroid-base checks over subsets of X reduce exactly to the latent set and each singleton augmentation.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Binary matrices with columns partitioned into L and X.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: Phase 2 imputes each observed column independently; Appendix A.2/A.4.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 10

evidence.anchor: Constructing a particular solution for singleton augmentation

equation_theory_inventory.summary: A circuit-based set D gives a deterministic replacement column preserving the full transversal matroid.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Known matroid of H and known latent-column submatroid.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 11
equation_theory_inventory.summary: An irreducible linear ICA representation has equal source count and proportional-column correspondence under non-Gaussianity.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Non-Gaussian components and irreducible ICA representations.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Known result quoted from Eriksson & Koivunen (2004); no proof here.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 12

evidence.anchor: The whole column augmentations can be traversed by edge additions/deletions

equation_theory_inventory.summary: The Hasse graph over all matroid-preserving column augmentations is weakly connected.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Any binary Q and replaceable column x.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: Supports edge-wise traversal of equivalence classes.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 13

evidence.anchor: When an edge in a bipartite graph can be altered without changing the transversal matroid

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Four conditions, including basis equality and a coloop rank inequality, are equivalent for a single edge alteration.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Binary support matrix and one absent edge.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 1

evidence.anchor: Determining items that must not appear in any solution

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Lemma 10’s circuit-derived D is the union, hence unique maximal inclusive element, of all valid column augmentations.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Solution set colaug(Q,x).
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Derived from Lemma 10; no separate proof block.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 2

evidence.anchor: Determining items that must appear in all solutions

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Minimum new cocircuits identify minimal solutions and their intersection identifies elements present in every solution.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Difference in cocircuits between Q and Q without x.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Complement argument; no separate proof block.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 3

evidence.anchor: Traverse all bipartite graphs that realize a transversal matroid

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Equal transversal matroids are connected by admissible edge changes followed by a column permutation, with a unique maximal reachable support.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Binary matrices inducing the same transversal matroid.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Derived from Lemma 12/Lemma 13; no separate proof block.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 4

evidence.anchor: Traverse all digraphs that realize the same matroid tower under latents

equation_theory_inventory.summary: Tower equality is equivalent to latent-block basis equality plus valid singleton augmentations for every observed source.
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Binary matrices with columns L ∪ X.
equation_theory_inventory.proof_location: Derived from Lemma 9 and Corollary 3; no separate proof block.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 1
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Uses OICA identifiability and Lemma 2 to reduce proportional columns to a path-rank condition, then separates latent-only and one-observed cases.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Proposition 2
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Shows maximal redundant latent removal implements proportional-column merging and uses condition B.3 for well-defined iteration.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 3
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Forward direction follows mixing closure and rank preservation; reverse direction uses strict gammoid isomorphism, the Fundamental Lemma, and general simplex-position representations.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 8
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Splits and combines matchings across disjoint column blocks.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 10
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Compares independent families in the cases where the latent block already has full rank and where the singleton adds rank.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 12
equation_theory_inventory.summary: D is maximal; any valid solution can add missing D elements one by one, yielding a directed path to D and weak connectivity.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 9
equation_theory_inventory.summary: A minimal matching disagreement in a multi-column augmentation projects to a singleton disagreement.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 13
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Establishes the cycle of implications among basis equality, rank equality, and the coloop condition.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Lemma 7
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Reduces edge alteration to the singleton matroid and rules out restoration by permutation when independent sets differ.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Proof of Theorem 3
equation_theory_inventory.summary: Combines column-augmentation connectivity, latent-column traversal, row permutation for nonzero diagonals, and latent relabeling.

claim_closure.claim: Arbitrary latent-variable cyclic LiNG models can be compared by observed distribution sets after irreducible canonicalization.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations (1)–(7), Definition 1, and the reduction procedure formalize models and remove trivial redundant latents.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Propositions 1–2 provide the graphical irreducibility condition and reduction proof in Appendix B.1.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 restates distributional equivalence for latent-variable LiNG models.

claim_closure.claim: Mixing-matrix closure and path ranks characterize equivalence.
claim_closure.method_response: Lemma 1 reduces equivalence to mixing sets up to scaling/permutation; Lemmas 2–3 connect generic ranks to path ranks.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B.2 proves both directions using strict gammoids and general simplex position.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 recalls the graphical characterization, while §4 refines it to edge ranks.

claim_closure.claim: Edge ranks fill a local rank-based tool and are dual to path ranks.
claim_closure.method_response: Definitions 4–6, Lemma 4, and Theorem 1 establish edge ranks, support matrices, matching ranks, and duality.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 1 is identified as a matroid result; Lemma 4 is immediate from definition, and Appendix B.5 records these proof dispositions.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 names edge rank constraints as central contribution.

claim_closure.claim: Theorem 2 gives a local graphical equivalence criterion.
claim_closure.method_response: Children bases in Eq. (18) reduce all observed-source subsets to L and each L∪{Xi}.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B.3.3 proves Lemma 9, the singleton reduction on which Theorem 2 rests.

claim_closure.claim: The whole equivalence class is traversable by admissible edge operations and cycle reversals.
claim_closure.method_response: Lemmas 6–7 and Theorem 3 define cycle reversals, coloop-based edge changes, and the at-most-one-cycle-reversal sequence.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B.3–B.4 derives Hasse connectivity, matroid traversal, and the final theorem.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 uses BFS/DFS traversal and §6 retains the model-up-to-equivalence claim.

claim_closure.claim: A CP(G)-style presentation exposes maximal and invariant edges within each cycle-reversal configuration.
claim_closure.method_response: Theorem 4 defines solid/dashed edges and a unique maximal graph for the edge-operation component.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix C.3 gives four properties and Figures 5–6, but future steps for edge-group bounds and prior knowledge are explicitly undeveloped.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The main conclusion does not revisit Theorem 4 or its unimplemented extensions.

evidence.anchor: Theorem 4 is deferred to Appendix C.3

claim_closure.claim: glvLiNG recovers the full equivalence class from data under oracle OICA and faithfulness.
claim_closure.method_response: OICA, two-phase rank realization, row permutation, and Theorem 3 traversal form the algorithmic chain.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix A gives faithfulness, transversal-matroid realization, singleton augmentation, and the graph interpretation; finite-sample OICA is heuristic.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 states recovery up to equivalence without structural assumptions, with OICA as the main limitation.

claim_closure.claim: The constraint-based realization scales better than MILP.
claim_closure.method_response: Phase 1 uses matroid realization and Phase 2 uses singleton constructions rather than integer programming.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 4 covers selected n, latent counts, and average degrees, with many MILP non-completions; no broad hardware or implementation sensitivity is shown.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 calls the algorithm efficient; §6 does not quantify the scope of the speed claim.

claim_closure.claim: Structural-assumption-free glvLiNG is more robust to dense graphs and latent dimensionality than baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: The method accepts arbitrary latent/observed edges and cycles at the model level.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 7 supports dense-graph and latent-dimensionality patterns only under specified Erdős–Rényi settings and SD curves.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No quantitative finite-sample claim is repeated in §6.

claim_closure.claim: The stock-market graph contains meaningful causal sources and latent interpretations.
claim_closure.method_response: glvLiNG and CP(G) presentation are applied to 14 stock returns.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 8 and its text provide descriptive graph patterns but no intervention, external validation, or uncertainty analysis.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The main conclusion omits this qualitative case.

claim_closure.claim: The result is the first structural-assumption-free parametric latent-variable equivalence characterization.
claim_closure.method_response: The paper gives a general LiNG graphical criterion and explicitly lists prior settings in Table 2.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The novelty comparison is literature-positioning rather than a finite exhaustive survey; Table 2 and C.5 establish scope but cannot test a universal first claim here.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 states the characterization without repeating the priority wording.

evidence.anchor: first equivalence characterization ... any parametric setting

claim_closure.claim: Edge-rank ideas should extend to Gaussian, discrete, and nonlinear settings.
claim_closure.method_response: The paper explains translation ideas for trek ranks, tensor ranks, and Jacobian ranks, without deriving a full new characterization.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix C.4–C.5 explicitly marks Gaussian sufficiency gaps and nonlinear rank estimation as future challenges.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 mentions extension to linear Gaussian systems as future work.

evidence.anchor: extending new tools to broader settings

final_judgment.single_storyline: 论文沿着一条「先定义可识别对象，再把全局路径秩局部化为边秩，最后实现等价类恢复」的主线推进。§2 用 LiNG mixing set 与 irreducibility 去除平凡不可识别；§3 由 path-rank 等价走向 edge-rank duality；§4 用 children bases 得到 Theorem 2，并用 admissible operations 得到 Theorem 3；§5 将这条链实现为 glvLiNG。证据位于 p.3–10、Appendix A–B p.19–35。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留模型定义、20 个主文公式、path/edge rank 链、Theorem 2–3、glvLiNG 三阶段概览和五类评价问题。Figure 1–3 用于 reduction、rank duality 和 class traversal；正文还明确 oracle OICA/faithfulness 条件与 OICA 效率边界。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: 附录承载 71 个字母编号公式、传递 matroid 基础、两阶段重建构造、10 个显式证明块、Theorem 4/CP(G) 展开、完整枚举/runtime/oracle/simulation/stock 结果。主文可理解方法和主要趋势，但复核证明、复现实验和不确定性必须查附录。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 最有效的模式是把全局难题逐步压缩：Lemma 1 的 mixing closure → Lemma 3 的 path ranks → Theorem 1 的 path/edge duality → Lemma 9/Theorem 2 的 singleton bases → Theorem 3 的局部变换。每一层都回答上一层的可操作性问题，Figure 2 和 Figure 3 提供结构直觉。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 最大缺口是理论主张与有限样本机制证据之间仍有条件断层：exact guarantee 依赖 oracle OICA 与 faithfulness；真实实验用启发式 noisy-rank 处理，未报告 rank-error、class-coverage 或 traversal failure；稠密图优势来自有限 Erdős–Rényi 设置，主文没有组件消融。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 涉及等价类或不可识别性的论文，应先把「观测对象 → 等价不变量 → 局部判定 → 类遍历」的因果链逐层闭合，再把算法、实验和限制绑定到同一不变量。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于有明确结构不变量和可构造等价类的理论/算法论文。若模型只有经验评分、等价关系无法观测，或实验不能区分机制，结论应停留在任务范围内的描述性效果，不能外推为普遍识别或因果保证。
